note: Suggestions for you to review. Nothing here has been decided. Each item lists the options; the 'Default in this build' is what the site does now, and it is reversible.

suggestions.question: How often should a new guide be published?

options.label: One guide every two weeks
options.argument: Enough to build a feed history; slow enough to check each guide against sources.

options.label: One guide per month
options.argument: Lowest maintenance; the feed will look sparse early on.

options.label: One guide per week
options.argument: Fastest feed growth; highest verification load per week.

suggestions.default_in_build: Five guides published on 2026-11-19. No further cadence set.
suggestions.unlocks: Calendar for the next topics; feed rhythm.

suggestions.question: Which link format should product buttons use?

options.label: Keep the supplied short links, marked sponsored
options.argument: Matches what was supplied. Credit to shopnow047c-20 is unconfirmed (FLAG-01).

options.label: Replace with Special Links after an Associates test
options.argument: Follows the Operating Agreement's Special Link definition. Needs one test per product in the Associates workflow first.

options.label: Use amazon.com/dp links with the tag after ASINs are confirmed
options.argument: Clear destination once FLAG-02 is closed. Needs the owner's confirmation of each ASIN.

suggestions.default_in_build: Option a. Links unchanged, rel="sponsored" on every one.

suggestions.question: Where should the analytics endpoint run, if anywhere?

options.label: Browser-only counts (current)
options.argument: No data leaves the browser. Gives no site-wide totals.

options.label: Self-host analytics-endpoint/server.py
options.argument: Site-wide counts by event and path. Needs a server you control and a privacy review.

options.label: Use a third-party privacy analytics product
options.argument: Less setup. Needs its own data-processing and consent review.

suggestions.default_in_build: Option a. Five events recorded in the visitor's browser only.
suggestions.unlocks: Measured queries and click totals; the campaign ledger.

suggestions.question: Which categories should the site cover?

options.label: Air fryers and ovens, plus meat thermometers
options.argument: Matches the five supplied links (FLAG-03).

options.label: Air fryers and ovens only
options.argument: Matches the air-fryer register; drops P4 and P5 from the public site.

options.label: Keep both, but publish the thermometer category later
options.argument: Holds P4 and P5 back until scope is confirmed.

suggestions.question: Where should product images come from?

options.label: No photography until a source is chosen
options.argument: Zero licensing risk. Pages stay text-led.

options.label: Amazon listing images, after checking Program Content terms
options.argument: Recognisable products. Terms are in the Operating Agreement (FLAG-09) and must be checked first.

options.label: Owner-taken photos
options.argument: Original images. Needs the owner to take them.

suggestions.question: What is the site's name, and who signs the guides?

options.label: Working name 'Kitchen Buyer's Desk', byline 'Editorial team'
options.argument: Neutral. Replace freely.

options.label: Owner's name or pen name, with a short bio
options.argument: Adds a person to the work. Needs the details and a bio.

suggestions.default_in_build: Option a, labelled as a working name.
suggestions.unlocks: Author pages and the About page.

suggestions.question: Which guide should come next, and on what evidence?

options.label: Choose from Search Console queries after they accrue
options.argument: Grounded in real queries (once FLAG-07 is closed).

options.label: Choose from the register's open questions
options.argument: Answers questions readers would ask about the five products now.

options.label: Choose from the owner's own list
options.argument: The owner knows the audience best.

suggestions.default_in_build: Option b, using the five guides already published.
